vulnerability: Missing ownership and tokenOut validation in updateOrder allows arbitrary order modification and collateral theft
reason: updateOrder fetches initPosId from initPosIds[msg.sender][_posId] but never checks that this initPosId equals order.initPosId. Any attacker with any existing position can pass their own _posId and a victim's active _orderId to overwrite the victim's order parameters, including triggerPrice, limitPrice, tokenOut, and collAmt. The function also fails to validate _tokenOut against the victim's baseAsset/quoteAsset, unlike _createOrder. The attacker can set _collAmt up to their own collateral, set tokenOut to a malicious token, and choose limitPrice so that amtOut calculated in fillOrder is zero or negligible. Then the attacker calls fillOrder on the victim's order: the function repays the victim's debt proportional to _collAmt and decollateralizes that amount of the victim's collateral to the attacker, while the attacker pays almost nothing of the malicious tokenOut to the victim. If the attacker's collateral is at least the victim's, they can set _collAmt to the victim's full collateral, repay the full debt, and steal the entire position equity, directly draining victim positions.

vulnerability: Missing health check in removeCollateral allows undercollateralized withdrawal and bad debt creation
reason: removeCollateral decollateralizes and burns _shares of collateral, sends all resulting underlying tokens to the caller, and only returns the post-operation health without enforcing any minimum. Unlike _reducePosInternal, which validates _minHealth_e18 via _validateHealth, this function has no health parameter or post-condition. A position owner can borrow via openPos or increasePos up to the allowed limit, then call removeCollateral with their full collateral shares. The collateral is returned to the owner while the debt remains. The owner can abandon the position, leaving the lending pool with bad debt. The attacker profits by keeping both the borrowed funds and the withdrawn collateral, draining the lending pool's liquidity.

vulnerability: Unprotected initializer allows attacker to set malicious swapHelper and steal funds
reason: initialize is external and protected only by the initializer modifier, with no access control. If the contract is not initialized atomically during deployment, an attacker can front-run the legitimate initialization and set swapHelper to a malicious contract. During any openPos, increasePos, or reducePos that performs a swap, coreCallback transfers the entire tokenIn balance held by the hook to swapHelper and calls IBaseSwapHelper(swapHelper).swap(swapInfo). A malicious swapHelper can simply keep the transferred tokens or return worthless tokens, stealing user funds. Because swapHelper has no setter after initialization, the attacker permanently compromises the contract's swapping functionality, making all subsequent swaps unsafe and directly profitable to the attacker.
